newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna stocks barely changed after earlier spurt.
newsitem.headline: Vienna stocks barely changed after earlier spurt.

text.p: Austrian shares ended barely changed on Wednesday after an early morning flurry of buying petered out and profit-taking kicked in, traders said.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips ended just 0.16 points, or 0.01 percent, higher at 1,076.16 after earlier climbing up to 1,083.93.
The earlier buying had been triggered by U.S. President Bill Clinton's election victory and the Republicans maintaining control of Congress.
"Sellers came in on highs," said one trader, who currently sees 1,080 points as a hurdle.
"In order to clear it we need a larger impetus from abroad, which I don't see happening for the time being."
Another trader said the EU's prospects of 1.6 percent growth next year for Austria's economy prompted some investors to sell shares.

"That's the second-lowest growth in the EU -- some could've used that as an incentive to get out," he said, adding he expects the ATX to be hemmed into a 1,060 to 1,080-point range for the short-term.
Of the 21 blue chips, 11 gained, seven fell and three were unchanged.
The day's best performer was AMS, rebounding another 1.40 percent to 722 schillings after last week's selling due to disappointing nine-month earnings.
The leading decliner was Creditanstalt preferred shares, down 1.45 percent to 503 schillings.
The all-share Vienna bourse index closed up just 0.01 points at 413.23.
The November ATX future shed 1.3 points to 1,076.2 on turnover of 1,080 contracts.
